docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Simple. Fast. Powerful. Simple data integration. High-performance. Rich features.

SDI is a data integration tool that seamlessly connects with Oracle / SQL Server / MySQL / PostgreSQL / DB2, cloud DWHs such as BigQuery / Snowflake, SaaS such as Salesforce, S3 / OCI Object Storage / GCP Cloud Storage / Azure Blob, and Web APIs. With the built-in scheduler and gateway, you can securely automate workflows within the same site, across multiple sites, and with cloud services.

Start Free Trial Contact Us Why SDI Licensing  Key Features Data Integration

Database-to-database integration Database–file integration Web services / Web API integration Execute SQL queries and stored procedures Incremental load

Workflow & Notifications

Workflow capability Chained execution of multiple tasks Automated scheduled report delivery Email / event notifications for run results

Scheduler & Triggers

Run hourly, at specific times, weekly, or monthly Run at fixed intervals Trigger on file create / update / delete Retry capability

Observability

Run history visualization Database availability monitoring Automatic detection of anomalies, missing data, and inconsistencies

SDI Gateway Service

Secure HTTPS-proxy connectivity across sites and clouds Zero-trust friendly

CLI

Controllable from batch scripts and external jobs Easy to embed into automation

 Supported Data Sources

SQL Server PostgreSQL DB2 ODBC Connection (RDB/SaaS) Salesforce Web API（REST） SOAP Web Service OData FTP FTPS SFTP S3 OCI Object Storage GCP Cloud Storage Azure Blob Storage CSV Excel JSON XML  Why SDI 1 Simple & Powerful

Set up in a few clicks. Complete integrations in as few as 3 steps. A simple UI with strong extensibility.

2 High-Performance Architecture

Parallelism, in-memory processing, and compressed transfer keep large volumes fast. Bottlenecks minimized.

3 Flexible Operations

Supports on-prem, cloud, and hybrid. Cold standby and automatic failover are available.

 Use Cases 1 Internal Systems integration

Integrate and unify data across different formats and RDBs. From master data and transactions through synchronization and aggregation.

2 Multi-site / multi-cloud integration

Bi-directional, multi-site & multi-cloud integration—keep data consistent across regions while syncing on-prem with public clouds.

3 Scheduled File Automation

Scheduled generation and auto-ingestion of CSV / Excel / JSON / XML. Supports S3 / Blob / Object Storage.

docs.text: SDI does not work on Linux operating system. Please refer to the following page for more information about the system requirements. System architecture / System requirements

docs.title: Q: Can SDI Worker Agents be configured for redundancy?
docs.text: Yes, it is possible. By utilizing an Active/Standby configuration with multiple servers and automatic failover, you can enhance business continuity and improve availability in the event of a failure.

docs.title: Q: Can SDI Gateway Services be configured for redundancy?
docs.text: Yes, redundancy can be achieved by using a load balancer in conjunction with multiple SDI Gateway Service instances.

docs.title: Q: Is stable operation possible even with large volumes of data?
docs.text:
Yes. In actual implementation cases, SDI has maintained stable operations while continuously performing data integration for millions of records per hour and high-frequency mapping execution (thousands of times per hour).

SDI is fully capable of handling significant scales of data integration while maintaining simple and intuitive operability.

docs.title: <userAuthentication>
docs.text:
Description

Only authenticated users can access the cdbc service. In this session, you can set the user authentication method and related settings.

<userAuthentication authMethod="None , Basic or UserPsk">

Attributes

Attribute Description Value Remarks authMethod User authorization method. None , Basic or UserPsk None - No user authorization. Any user can access the service.Basic - Use IIS basic authorization. Cdbc will not do user authentication. UserPsk - Use Pre-Shared Key for each user.

docs.title: <authenticatedUsers>
docs.text:
Description

The authenticated user list can be stored in the authenticatedUsers section. You can use the AuthenticatedUsersCollection to retrieve authenticated users from application configuration files. Its properties map to authenticated user attributes, allowing you to retrieve a single authenticated user specifying the userId. This setting is valid only when userAuthentication authMethod = "UserPsk"

<authenticatedUsers>
  <add userId="" userPsk="" comment=""/>
</authenticatedUsers>

Attributes

Attribute Description Value Remarks userId User ID String userPsk User psk (Pre-Shared Key 16 digital) String comment Comment about the user, It will not be used by the system String

docs.title: <clientApplicationAuthentication>
docs.text:
Description

Only the authenticated client application can access cdbc service. You can configure client application authorization method and related settings in this session.

    <clientApplicationAuthentication authMethod="None or ApplicationPsk">

Attributes

Attribute Description Value Remarks authMethod Client application authorization method. None - No application authentication. All applications can access the service. ApplicationPsk - Use a Pre-Shared Key for each application.

docs.text:

This setting is valid only when clientApplicationAuthentication authMethod = "ApplicationPsk"

      <authenticatedApplications>

      </authenticatedApplications>

docs.title: <idps>
docs.text:
Description

Idps is used to block illegal access. The accesses will be blocked for a specified time period while authorization failed certain time.

        <idps enabled="true" 
          accessBlockApplicationFailureCount="5"           
          accessBlockUserFailureCount="5" 
          accessBlockIpAdressFailureCount="20" 
          accessBlockSeconds="10" 
          failureResetSeconds="600"  />
Attributes

Attribute Description Value Remarks enabled Enable or disable Idps. If Idps is enabled , Cdbc service will block the accesses after authorization failed certain times. true or false default true accessBlockApplicationFailureCount Used to set the application authorization failure count while start block. int>=1 default 5 Count access from same ip and same application id accessBlockUserFailureCount Used to set the user authorization failure count while start block. int>=1 default 5 Count access from same ip and same user id accessBlockIpAdressFailureCount Used to set the authorization failure count from the same ip while start to block access. int>=1 default 20 Count access from same ip accessBlockSeconds Used to set how many seconds will the access be blocked. int>=1 default 10 failureResetSeconds If there is no authorization error after a certain seconds the failure count will be reset to 0. failureResetSeconds is used to set the reset time. int>accessBlockSeconds default 600

docs.title: 1. Stop execution and back up
docs.text:
Stop Workers and CLI executions on every computer and verify in Execution Log that active tasks have finished. Stopping an agent does not cancel tasks already executing. Close Studio as well.

Back up the configuration folder, each computer's local SdiWorkerBasic.config, and any required logs. Retain the customer-managed key separately. A system-managed key's local settings are computer-specific and cannot be restored to another computer merely by copying them.

docs.title: 2. Uninstall the previous version and install the new version
docs.text:
1. Select SimpleDataIntegrator in Windows Programs and Features and uninstall it.
  2. Run the supplied new-version SimpleDataIntegratorSetup.msi.
  3. Follow the installer. Keep Worker and CLI stopped until settings have been verified.

docs.title: 3. Verify settings in Studio
docs.text:
1. Open Studio and select the existing configuration folder.
  2. Verify existing connections and credentials.
  3. Register the same customer-managed key on every computer sharing the configuration.
  4. If the key or identity cannot be read, follow recovery instructions. Preserve existing files rather than deleting and recreating them.

docs.title: 4. Review API incremental positions
docs.text: Review the incremental position when API retrieval conditions change. Follow incremental API retrieval to reapply the saved UTC position, specify another UTC boundary, or clear it. Clearing restarts from the default date.

docs.title: 5. Verify operation and resume
docs.text: Test existing connections and representative mappings in Studio. Start the SimpleDataIntegratorWorker Windows service and verify tasks under its normal service account. If CLI is used, verify execution from CLI too. Resume cluster operation only after key registration and connection checks on every node.

docs.title: Cluster Configuration
docs.text: Use cluster configuration to assign schedules to Primary and Secondary nodes and select Active-Standby or Active-Active operation. This feature is available in Enterprise Edition and Developer Edition. The cluster tab appears when multiple agents are configured.

docs.title: Configure the cluster
docs.text:
1. Configure each computer's Worker agent and the shared configuration folder in System Settings.
  2. Select Active-Standby for standby redundancy, or Active-Active for concurrent operation.
  3. Filter schedules by name or group if needed.
  4. Select schedules and use >> or << to move assignments between Primary and Secondary.
  5. Save the configuration. Use Undo to discard unsaved changes.

docs.title: Management keys and initialization
docs.text:
Select a customer-managed key and register the same key on every computer sharing the configuration. Copying shared files does not replace local key registration.

Initialize and register keys through Studio on each computer. Before changing keys, stop all Workers and CLI executions and wait for active work to finish. Save the change on one computer, register the same key on the remaining computers, and verify every node before resuming operation. See management keys.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The connection configuration form is used to set up connections for various databases (Oracle, SQL Server, etc.), files (Excel, CSV, JSON, XML), and web services or web APIs.

docs.title: Composition of connection configuration form
docs.text: No Item Description 1 Basic information Basic information such as connection name, location, type, etc. 2 Connection details Enter detailed connection information to connect to DBs. 3 Buttons

docs.title: Basic information
docs.text: No Item Description 1 Connection Name Enter a name identifying the connection. 2 Description Describe its purpose or destination. 3 Group Select a group used to organize connections. 4 Group maintenance Open the group creation, editing, and deletion form. 5 Location Select direct database access, File, Web Service/API, remote database through Gateway Service, or SaaS. 6 Data Type Select a database or file format for the location. Its connection details then appear. 7 Show passwords and secrets Show or hide credentials in this form.

docs.title: Show or hide passwords
docs.text:
Use Show passwords and secrets to toggle masked values such as passwords and API keys in this form. Values are hidden initially. The visibility state is not saved and is reset when the form is opened again.

When Studio authentication is enabled, each reveal requires the Studio authentication password. Canceling the confirmation keeps the values hidden.

The same control is available in Mail Settings. For ZIP attachments in mapping mail processing, see ZIP password visibility. Hide values again before sharing or capturing the screen.

docs.title: Headers, cookies, and token lifetime
docs.text:
Custom headers in Web Request Details are sent for GET, POST, and subsequent pages. Authentication configured on the connection takes precedence over manually specified authentication headers. With Anonymous authentication, a manually configured Authorization header can be used. Invalid headers cause an error.

Cookies are retained across pages of the same API execution. They are not shared with another execution or connection.

OAuth tokens follow the response's expires_in. If a JWT exp is also available, the earlier expiration is used, with renewal before expiry. If neither expiration can be determined, the token is fetched again instead of being cached for a fixed duration.

For date-based Web API extraction, see incremental API retrieval.

docs.text: SDI mail templates support both text and HTML. If the template body contains basic HTML tags, it will be sent as HTML; if not, it will be sent as plain text.

docs.title: 1) Basics of Placeholder Variables
docs.text:
• Enclose variables in curly braces {}.
  • At runtime, SDI replaces them with values.
  • Main system variables (examples):
Variable Name Definition Description {DateTime} Current date and time {WorkerAgentName} Worker agent name {MappingId} Mapping ID {MappingName} Mapping Name {SchedulerName} Scheduler Name {Message} Detailed message when sent by the system Specify at runtime {ErrorMessage} Error message when an error occurs Inserted only on errors {OutputFile} Contents of the exported text file Use when you want to display the output file’s contents as plain text in the email body. {AddInformation1} Additional info 1 Set on the Mapping Details page {AddInformation2} Additional info 2 Set on the Mapping Details page {AddInformation3} Additional info 3 Set on the Mapping Details page

docs.title: 2) Automating Dates/Periods (Safe Subset)
docs.text:
A safe subset that evaluates dates only inside { ... } is available (arbitrary code execution is not allowed).

Commonly usable expressions:

  • Roots: DateTime.Now / DateTime.UtcNow / DateTime.Today
  • Additions: .AddYears(n), .AddMonths(n), .AddDays(n), .AddHours(n), .AddMinutes(n), etc.
  • Start/End helpers: .StartOfMonth(), .EndOfMonth(), .StartOfWeek() (depends on environment implementation)
  • Formatting: .ToString("format"[, "culture"])

Example (Subject): Monthly Sales Summary ({DateTime.Now.AddMonths(-1).ToString("yyyy-M")})

docs.title: Staging table details
docs.text:
For an RDB target, open Mapping Advanced Settings, then Detail under Load Into Staging Table. A staging table holds extracted data before the target is updated.

No Item Description 1 Table type Oracle offers Regular table, Temporary table (PRIVATE), and Temporary table (GLOBAL). 2 Explanation Describes the scope and restrictions of the selected type. 3 Execute SQL Prior to Data Loading Configure SQL before loading. docs.title: Choosing a table type
docs.text:
Destination Choices Usage Oracle, direct connection Regular / PRIVATE / GLOBAL Regular tables persist. PRIVATE definitions and data belong to this execution. GLOBAL definitions are shared, with data isolated to each connection. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, direct connection Regular / Temporary Temporary tables are used within the creating connection. Oracle’s PRIVATE/GLOBAL choices are not shown. BigQuery, Snowflake Regular / Temporary on supported connections Uses the database product’s temporary tables. Available choices depend on the connection type. Other databases or connection types Available settings only Temporary creation is not offered for every DB2 or arbitrary ODBC connection.

The non-Oracle example uses the same numbers: 1 table type, 2 explanation, 3 pre-load SQL. Do not depend on temporary data surviving across connections or being accessible to a separate mapping. Specify PostgreSQL temporary table names without a schema.

docs.title: Oracle PRIVATE
docs.text:
Requires Oracle 18c or later. SDI uses ON COMMIT PRESERVE DEFINITION, so a commit during execution does not remove the definition. Loading and target updates use the same connection. SDI removes the table when execution ends, including cleanup before a pooled connection is returned for reuse.

PRIVATE does not support mapped CLOB, NCLOB, or BLOB columns. Choose GLOBAL or a regular table when these columns must be written. Unmapped LOB columns on the target do not prevent PRIVATE use.

Physical names use Oracle’s private-table prefix, normally ORA$PTT_, without a schema. SDI uses the database prefix when it can read it. If a custom prefix is configured but unavailable to the connection, specify a complete ORA$... name that complies with the database rule. Keep the physical name within 128 bytes.

PRIVATE cannot be retained across executions. The data-retention checkbox is hidden. The parent Drop Staging Table setting stays visible but disabled and is treated as automatic cleanup. Do not access the table from a later connection or a Processor on Success action.

docs.title: Oracle GLOBAL
docs.text:
SDI creates the table with ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS. The definition is shared, but loaded data belongs to its database session. For a newly created table that is not retained, SDI commits or rolls back the target update, clears the stage in the original loading session, closes that connection, then drops the definition.

Consequently, stage rows are already cleared when Processor on Success runs. Put SQL that needs these rows in Postprocessor of update. If another session is using the same GLOBAL table, Oracle may reject DROP. SDI records a cleanup warning and does not terminate the other session. Avoid competing staging names in concurrent executions.

docs.title: Regular tables and retention
docs.text:
For regular tables, leaving Keep existing data unchecked clears existing rows before loading. Checking it retains those rows while loading. This is separate from the parent Drop Staging Table setting.

Even when dropping is enabled, SDI’s completion cleanup drops only a table created by that operation. It does not drop a table that already existed before execution.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This page describes the advanced settings for data acquisition from Salesforce, as well as the settings for saving execution results and writing back Salesforce IDs to the source database after data updates (such as Upsert).

By outputting an update result file, you can record success/failure, error details, and Salesforce IDs, which can be utilized for operational monitoring and troubleshooting. Additionally, by reflecting the Salesforce ID assigned or confirmed on the Salesforce side back into a specific column of the source database, you can ensure smooth subsequent updates and data reconciliation.

docs.title: Salesforce Advanced Settings (For Source)

This is suitable for large-scale objects or full data extraction, as it can extract large volumes of data (tens of thousands of records or more) quickly and efficiently.Use Bulk API (Disabled)Data is acquired using the standard Salesforce APIs (REST / SOAP). This is suitable for small data volumes where real-time performance is prioritized.

Use this when you want to write back the Salesforce ID to the source DB after an Upsert.Do not update: The ID column in the source DB is not updated.Update: Updates the specific column in the source DB with the Salesforce ID obtained from the update results (configured in [Detailed Settings]).

docs.title: Open the details
docs.text:
Configure the output value and transformation steps for each target column. Check Include, then click the detail icon in Value / transform.

A configured icon has a check mark. Clearing Include retains its settings but excludes the column from editing and execution.

docs.title: Configure values and transformations
docs.text:
Select an operation in 1 and add it. Select its row and configure 2. Enter samples and use 3, Preview conversion. Click the image for full size.

See the Transformation reference for all 24 operations, purposes, configured examples, and detail dialogs.

Goal Transformation Hide part of a value, such as a phone number Masking. If the retained length reaches the input length, the whole input is masked. Conceal values while keeping equal inputs matchable Hashing. Normally choose HMAC-SHA256 (SDI management key) and a string destination of at least 64 characters.

See Choosing a hash algorithm for the differences between algorithms and Consistent results across mappings and servers for sharing requirements.

docs.title: Value source
docs.text:
Mode Configuration Source Select an ordinary source column or an API bind source such as BIND:id. Constant Specify a String, Number, Boolean, DateTime, or Null value. System Select MappingStartTime, RowUuid, or RunUuid.

Enter string constants without quotation marks. Use String for 001 when leading zeros matter. An empty string and NULL are different values. Null does not use a text field.

Only fields relevant to the chosen mode are shown. Switching modes retains drafts within the dialog; only the selected mode is saved and executed. The mapping start time and run UUID are shared within one mapping execution, including per-input-row processing.

The mapping grid summarizes constants and system values in its source cell. Use the detail icon to edit them.

docs.title: Steps and output
docs.text:
1. Select an operation and click Add.
  2. Select its row, then set Input value, Result name, and operation-specific options.
  3. Set Value to output to the value that should be written to the target column.
Input / value mode Meaning Origin The configured value source: source column, constant, or system value. Column An unmodified source value. Select the column from Reference. Bind The API bind value passed to the request. Select its variable name. Literal A typed fixed value. StepResult The result of an earlier enabled step. Select its step name.

Use “…” on Input value or a parameter to configure the acquisition mode. Column, Bind, and StepResult use Reference; Literal uses its type and value. Origin does not require a reference or literal value.

Concat and Coalesce use the individual entries in Values to concatenate as their inputs. Add an Origin entry if you want the configured value source included. Condition operations likewise read their configured condition and branch values.

Each result is retained while processing that input row. You can transform several source columns independently and reference their results later; see combine independent results. Source values and other target columns are not modified.

Value to output selects Origin or an enabled step result. Only results required by that output and its dependencies are evaluated. A preview step marked as not used is not needed by the selected output.

docs.title: Reorder, disable, and delete
docs.text:
Up and Down move the selected step. Clearing Enabled disables it. A row’s trash icon deletes that row. Answering No in the confirmation retains the steps and output selection.

When deleting the physical last row that is also the output, the output moves to the nearest preceding enabled step. With no enabled steps remaining, it returns to Origin. The confirmation names the replacement output. An output already pointing elsewhere stays unchanged.

You cannot delete or disable a result used by another step, or move a consumer before its dependency. To delete a non-final output step, first choose another output.

docs.title: Example: delete an intermediate step
docs.text:
Suppose step 1 (Concat) feeds step 2 (Upper), which feeds step 3 (Replace blanks and NULL). To delete step 2, first change the reference in step 3.

  1. Select step 3, Replace blanks and NULL, and click “…” for Input value under Transformation options.
  2. Choose StepResult and change Reference from step 2 (Upper) to step 1 (Concat), then click OK.
  3. Click the trash icon at the right end of step 2 and choose Yes in the confirmation.
  4. Use Preview conversion to check the result after deletion.

This example passes the concatenated result directly to step 3, skipping uppercase conversion. You can choose Origin, a source column, or another input instead, depending on the desired result.

If several settings reference the step, change all references before deleting it. Check Input value as well as references inside Values to concatenate, conditions, replacement values, and other parameters. If Value to output selects the intermediate step being deleted, change that selection too. References are not automatically redirected to the preceding step.

docs.title: Preview with samples
docs.text:
Set Input type and Sample input for each reference, then choose Preview conversion. The results show the origin, step results, and final output.

String results are quoted so that empty strings, whitespace, numbers, and NULL can be distinguished. Select sample type Null to supply NULL; typing the String NULL is different.

In an example table, VALUE = "abc" means choose String as Input type for the VALUE row and enter only abc in Sample input. Do not enter VALUE = or quotation marks. Typing \t or \n into Sample input does not insert an actual tab or line break. The Tab key moves to the next cell.

See Sample notation and actual input for empty strings, whitespace, NULL, and the different interpretation used by regular-expression fields.

Preview performs no API calls, database updates, or configuration writes. Samples and preview results are not saved as part of the mapping.

docs.title: On conversion error
docs.text:
Policy Behavior Fail Report a conversion error and follow normal mapping error handling. Null Use NULL as this column’s result. Default Use the specified typed default as this column’s result.

Default type and value are shown only for Default. A Null default does not use a text input. An explicitly NULL value or NULL fallback cannot be configured for a non-nullable target.

Examples of errors include invalid date formats, an out-of-range substring, and an unmatched code. See the operation notes in the Transformation reference.

docs.title: Apply, save, and remove settings
docs.text:
OK applies the detail settings to the mapping form. Save on the mapping form writes them to the configuration file.

Cancel, the titlebar close button, and Esc use the same save confirmation as other settings forms when there are changes. Yes validates and applies to the mapping form, No discards, and Cancel resumes editing. Unchanged settings and sample-only edits do not prompt.

Remove value settings asks for confirmation before removing the column’s value and transformation settings and restoring its source mapping. The configuration file is unchanged until the mapping form is saved.

Refreshing columns on the same destination retains settings for matching target names. Changing the connection or RDB table does not transfer them automatically.

docs.title: Execution notes
docs.text:
• Columns without value settings output their selected source column.
  • Zero source rows produce zero output rows even when constants are configured.
  • Source-read whitespace trimming or empty-value normalization occurs before these transformations.
  • When a mapping supplies input to a later mapping, it supplies extracted source values, not another target column’s transformed results.
  • Raw-file output does not support column value settings.
  • With per-input-row retrieval and output, earlier rows may already have been written when a later row fails.

docs.text:
The source data can be selected from a database, Web Service / Web API, Salesforce, or a CSV, Excel, JSON, or XML file.

Complete the connection configuration before configuring the mapping.

If no filter is specified, all records are retrieved; otherwise, only records matching the filter are retrieved.Incremental extraction: Retrieves only records added or updated since the previous extraction. docs.title: Incremental Extraction
docs.text:
Retrieves only data updated since the previous extraction. Supported sources are Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, and Salesforce.

No Item Description A1 Update Timestamp Column Specify the reference column used to identify incremental changes. In addition to an update timestamp column, Oracle SCN (such as ORA_ROWSCN) can be used. Data updated since the previous extraction is retrieved using the specified reference value. A2 TimeZone Specify the time zone applied to the update timestamp column. A3 Last Update Timestamp Displays the last reference value (timestamp or SCN) used by the previous extraction. docs.title: Incremental Extraction Watermark Settings
docs.text:
Use this form to view and change the watermark used for incremental extraction. Clear the watermark or set it to a specific date and time to adjust the starting point. When Oracle SCN is used, the specified date and time are converted automatically to an SCN. If no UTC indication is displayed, the time is interpreted as the connected database's local time.

No Item Description B1 Current Watermark Displays the saved incremental extraction watermark: a timestamp for timestamp-based extraction or an SCN value for Oracle SCN-based extraction. B2 Clear Watermark Clear the existing watermark. The next database execution is treated as an initial run, subject to the configured extraction filter. For Web APIs, see incremental API retrieval below. B3 Set to Specified Time Set the watermark to a specified date and time (or its Oracle SCN equivalent) to resume incremental extraction from that point. B5 New Start Date Specify the extraction start date. When Oracle SCN is used, the date and time are converted internally to an SCN. B6 New Start Time Specify the extraction start time. Together with the date, it defines the starting reference value. B7 Time Zone Displays the time zone of the specified date and time. A UTC indication means UTC; otherwise, the connected database's local time is used. B8 Apply Update the watermark with the specified value. For Oracle SCN, convert the date and time to an SCN and save it as the starting point. B9 Cancel Discard the changes and close the form without updating the watermark.

docs.title: Bind Variable Settings
docs.text: Simple Data Integrator can use the SELECT results of one mapping as input (bind variables) for another mapping, enabling dynamic data integration between mappings.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Assign the SELECT results of an upstream input mapping to the bind variables of a downstream mapping. The downstream mapping then processes data using those values. Multiple parameters and multiple input rows are supported.

docs.title: Input mapping execution
docs.text:
• When upstream mapping A is called as input for downstream mapping B, A's normal target output is skipped.
  • Add only downstream mapping B to the scheduler. B calls A automatically.

docs.title: Configuration Steps
docs.text:
1. Enter bind variables in the extraction filter or query.

No Item Description 7 Filter Use bind variables in the extraction condition. Do not enter the WHERE keyword in the filter field.Example: UPDATE_TIME >= :latest_date. 9 Query Content Use the appropriate bind variable syntax in the SQL.Example:SELECT EMPID,EMPNAME,DEPT_CODEFROM HR.EMPWHERE DEPT_CODE = :DEPT_CODE

The bind variable syntax depends on the database:

Database Bind Variable Syntax Example Oracle :param SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id AND status = :status SQL Server @param SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = @id AND status = @status PostgreSQL @param SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = @id AND status = @status MySQL @param SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = @id AND status = @status DB2 @param SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = @id AND status = @status ODBC ? SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ? AND status = ?

2. Configure the bind variable details.

Click the Bind Variable Settings button to open the detailed settings form.

No Item Description P1 Bind Variable Values Select how to assign bind values.Use input mapping output (pass bind values): Bind each parameter to a value from the input mapping's results. These values are passed dynamically as SQL conditions or arguments.Do not use input mapping (execute fixed SQL): Execute using fixed values or database-specific variables defined in the SQL, without an input mapping. P2 Input Mapping Select the mapping that provides the bind variable values. P3 Processing Unit Process all rows together: Loop through the input mapping's rows, retrieve data for each row, and accumulate the results locally. After all data has been retrieved, perform downstream operations such as target database updates or file output once for the combined results.Process one row at a time (repeat): Retrieve data for each input row and perform downstream operations for that row immediately. P4 Input Column Select the column containing the value to bind to the parameter. P5 Bind Select whether to bind the parameter to the input column's value. When checked, the value is used as a condition or argument during extraction. When unchecked, the parameter is executed as a database-specific variable.This option is selectable only for SQL Server. P6 Parameter Type Set the bind variable's data type. P7 Group Filter Optionally filter the mapping list by group.

docs.title: For JSON
Identifying the record object (JSON and XML)
docs.text:
SDI identifies and saves the selected object by its path from the root. Arrays with the same name under different parents remain separate. Columns come from the selected location, and all elements at that path are retrieved. Reopening the mapping restores the same location.

For example, data.humanResourceRequirements.data.optionalList and data.skillRequirements.data.optionalList identify different arrays. Selecting the skill array exposes skillCategory, skillItem, and requiredLevel. Select the array itself to retrieve each element as a record.

After retrieving a structure, select the array to import in the tree, then choose Get Column Detail. Each array element becomes one record, and its fields become source column choices. If a record-object error appears, check the loaded structure and the selected location.

For JSON API page-number and offset paging, the selected array’s count determines whether paging has ended. An empty array is zero records. A missing object or a null value produces an error rather than falling back to another array, and does not advance the watermark.

docs.title: Pass input mapping values into an API path
docs.text:
For Web APIs returning JSON or XML, insert SDI’s {bind:name} token in the endpoint path. SDI supplies its value from the input mapping’s extracted source data, not from that mapping’s target transformations.

Let A be the input mapping and B the downstream mapping that uses A's values in its API path:

  • When A is called as input for B, A's normal target output is skipped.
  • Add only downstream mapping B to the scheduler. B calls A automatically.
/v1/orders/{bind:id}
  1. Prepare an input mapping that retrieves IDs, such as the Get IDs mapping shown below.
  2. Enter {bind:id} in the detail endpoint. Bind Parameters appears.
  3. Open it, select the input mapping, and map its ID column to API variable id. Column and variable names need not match.
  4. Choose the output mode and select the response’s record object.
  5. Expand columns, configure the target, save, and run the mapping.

No Item Configuration 1 Input mapping Select the mapping supplying the values. The group filter can narrow the list. 2 Output mode Combine results, or retrieve and output separately for each input row. 3 Input column → API variable name Map ID to id in this example. Mode Behavior Combine all retrieved results into one output (Batch) Call the API for each input row, then write all results together. A retrieval failure prevents output from starting. Retrieve and output for each input row (PerRow) Retrieve and output for each input row. Failed rows are reported and processing continues with later rows; the overall result is an error.

Both modes call the API for each input row. PerRow also repeats pre/post processing, pre-update deletion, and file writing per input row. Avoid overwriting the same file or deleting earlier rows’ results. Use Batch to combine all IDs into one output. Zero input rows produce no downstream API calls or output. Paging starts afresh for each input row.

API input mapping is required when bind tokens are used.

Variable names start with an ASCII letter or _, followed by ASCII letters, digits, or _. Names are case-sensitive. Repeated occurrences of a name use the same value. NULL, empty or whitespace-only values, / or \, and values producing . or .. path segments are rejected before sending. Supply unencoded values; SDI URL-encodes the variable portion.

Bind tokens are supported only in the URL path, not the host, query string, headers, or request body. Raw response-file output is not supported with input binding. Combine path binds with expressions for dates and the incremental retrieval start time:

/order/{bind:id}?date={yyyyMMdd}&since={LastWatermarkUTCTime.ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")}

{bind:LastWatermarkUTCTime} means an input variable, while {LastWatermarkUTCTime} reads the saved incremental retrieval start time. Input values are never evaluated again as expressions. A bound mapping shares one watermark across all input rows and advances it only after the whole operation succeeds.

docs.title: Use a bind value as a source column
docs.text:

Source Example target Value BIND:id ORDERID The input value used for this API call code CODE A field under the selected response detail object

The bind value is the string before URL encoding. Every detail and page returned for the same input row receives that value in either Batch or PerRow mode. The same variable can populate several target columns. Selecting only bind columns preserves the response record count; an empty detail array does not create a bind-only row. Structure sample values are never used for execution.

Adding bind choices requires no API call and also works with a file-loaded structure. A fixed query value such as unit=1 is not a bind column. Removing or renaming an endpoint variable marks source columns that reference it as undefined. Select the variable to use again before saving or executing the mapping.

docs.title: Incremental retrieval for Web APIs
docs.text:
Use expressions containing LastWatermarkLocalTime or LastWatermarkUTCTime in the endpoint or a fixed POST text body to retrieve data from the saved position. Enclose each expression in {} and preserve the variable name's case.

Variable Value LastWatermarkUTCTime The previously saved retrieval boundary in UTC. LastWatermarkLocalTime The same instant converted to the executing server's local time zone. Studio, Worker, and CLI use the time zone of their own execution server.

URL examples:

/api/v1/orders?updatedFrom={LastWatermarkUTCTime.ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")}
/api/v1/orders?updatedDate={LastWatermarkLocalTime.ToString("yyyyMMdd")}
/api/v1/orders?updatedFrom={LastWatermarkUTCTime.AddDays(-1).ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")}

Fixed POST text body (JSON):

{
  "updatedFrom": "{LastWatermarkUTCTime.AddMinutes(-5).ToString(\"yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ\")}",
  "status": "active"
}

Keep ordinary quotes in the URL expression; escape quotes as \" inside a JSON string. Use the format ending in Z with the UTC variable. A date-only format omits the time; the API's comparison rules also determine the retrieval range.

This feature is enabled by the source endpoint or a fixed POST text body. It does not enable incremental retrieval through headers, SQL-generated bodies, or OData. The API must support filtering by a date/time boundary.

docs.title: Set the incremental position
docs.text:
The source form displays the incremental position button when a supported variable is used. The position cannot be edited while the mapping is running.

No Item Description 1 Current watermark Displays the saved UTC boundary, or indicates that it is not set for the first run. 2 Clear watermark Remove the saved value. The next execution uses 2000/01/01 00:00:00 UTC. 3 Set to a specified time Save the specified UTC date and time. 4 New start date Enter the starting date. 5 New start time Enter the starting time. 6 UTC The display and input time zone. Enter UTC even when using the Local variable. 7 Apply Confirm and apply the clear or set operation. 8 Cancel Close without changing the position.

docs.title: Save timing and replay
docs.text:
An unset or cleared API watermark uses the default boundary. Unlike the DB watermark clear operation, this does not necessarily retrieve all records. The configured date filter and the API determine the actual range.

Within one execution, the previous watermark is fixed across all pages. The new candidate boundary is the UTC time immediately before the first API request. It is saved after all pages and downstream processing succeed; failure, warning, or cancellation does not advance it. When the API mapping supplies another mapping's input, its watermark is saved after downstream success. Preview and access tests do not advance the execution watermark.

To overlap retrieval for late-arriving records, move the filter boundary back, for example with .AddMinutes(-5). Configure target keys and update behavior to handle repeated records.

docs.title: Changing API retrieval conditions
docs.text:
If the base URL, endpoint, method, POST body, headers, or other recorded retrieval conditions differ from the saved conditions, execution stops for confirmation of the position.

  1. Review the changed API conditions and decide which UTC boundary to use.
  2. Save the mapping and open the incremental position dialog.
  3. To continue from the same position, reapply the displayed UTC date and time. To retrieve a different period, set the required UTC boundary.
  4. Clear the position to restart from the default boundary.
  5. Execute again and verify the retrieved range and results.

Sample input Final result VALUE = "A,B,C" "B"

Notes

The index starts at 1 and includes empty items: item 2 of A,,C is empty. Separator is a literal string, not a regex. This operation does not create additional rows or columns.

For example, requesting item 3 of aaa_bbb with separator _ causes a conversion error with Raise an error, or returns NULL with Return NULL. A later Replace blanks and NULL step can replace that NULL with a chosen value. An existing empty item remains an empty string regardless of this choice.

An index of 0 or less, or an empty separator, remains a configuration error. The form's On conversion error setting handles errors raised by Raise an error and other conversion failures.

docs.title: ConvertType
docs.text:
Convert values to another type, such as numeric text to Number.

Configure

Set Output type to Number, Culture to en-US, and Allow numeric group separators to True. Keep the sample input type String.

Setting Example Output type Number Culture (empty for invariant) en-US Allow numeric group separators True

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = "1,234.50" 1234.50

Notes

Output types are String, Number, Boolean, DateTime, and Null. An empty culture uses invariant formatting. Boolean conversion accepts true, false, 1, and 0. DateTime adds input-format and time-zone options. Use the DateTime transformation to create a date string with an explicit output format.

docs.title: DateTime
docs.text:
Configure date formatting, time-zone conversion, and date arithmetic.

Configure

Set Input format mode to Exact, Input format to yyyyMMdd, and Date only to True. Set Output mode to String and Output format to yyyy-MM-dd.

Setting Example Culture (empty for invariant) empty Input format mode Exact Input format yyyyMMdd Date only True Input time zone UTC Output time zone Keep Output mode String Output format yyyy-MM-dd Years to add 0 Months to add 0 Days to add 0 Hours to add 0 Minutes to add 0 Seconds to add 0

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = "20240401" "2024-04-01"

Input and output options are in the same property panel. Scroll it to reach Output mode and Output format.

Additions apply in year, month, day, hour, minute, second order before output-zone conversion. Negative values subtract; Days to add = 1 selects the next day.

For time-zone conversion, input 2024-04-01T00:00:00Z, Output time zone = Tokyo Standard Time, and Output format = yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:sszzz produce 2024-04-01 09:00:00+09:00. An input Z or offset takes precedence; otherwise Input time zone is used. Keep preserves the input offset. Choose UTC for a Z-suffixed output. Invalid or ambiguous daylight-saving times cause errors.

Notes

MM means month, mm means minute, and HH uses a 24-hour clock. Custom formats are accepted. Typed output does not use Output format. For Date only, keep the output time zone as Keep and hours/minutes/seconds additions at 0.

docs.title: Calculate
docs.text:
Calculate using two values, such as unit price multiplied by quantity.

Configure

Use VALUE as the unit price, select Multiply, and open Operand with “…”. Choose Column and select QUANTITY.

Setting Example Arithmetic operation Multiply Operand QUANTITY

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = 1200QUANTITY = 3 3600

In child area 1, set the mode, reference, literal type, and value as applicable; use 2, OK, to return. Column and Bind references use the dropdown. Literal values do not use Reference.

Notes

Operations are Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, and Remainder. Subtraction and division use input minus/divided by operand. A NULL input or operand produces NULL. Division/remainder by zero and numeric overflow cause errors.

docs.title: Round
docs.text:
Round a number to a specified number of decimal places.

Configure

Set Precision value to the Number literal 2 and Rounding mode to AwayFromZero. Precision may also come from a column or earlier result.

Setting Example Precision value Constant: 2 Rounding mode AwayFromZero

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = 123.455 123.46

In child area 1, set the mode, reference, literal type, and value as applicable; use 2, OK, to return. Column and Bind references use the dropdown. Literal values do not use Reference.

Notes

Precision is 0–28 decimal places. AwayFromZero rounds midpoint values away from zero; ToEven chooses the even last digit. For 123.445 at two places, the results are 123.45 and 123.44 respectively.

docs.title: Ceiling
docs.text:
Return the smallest integer greater than or equal to the input.

Configure

Select a numeric column or calculation result as Input value. Ceiling has no additional operation-specific options.

There are no operation-specific fields. Check the input value and selected output step.

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = 12.3 13

Notes

This rounds to an integer; it does not accept a decimal-place parameter. A negative value such as -12.3 becomes -12, rounding toward positive infinity.

docs.title: Floor
docs.text:
Return the largest integer less than or equal to the input.

Configure

Select a numeric column or calculation result as Input value. Floor has no additional operation-specific options.

There are no operation-specific fields. Check the input value and selected output step.

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = 12.9 12

Notes

Floor rounds toward negative infinity rather than simply removing the fractional part. -12.3 becomes -13. Use Round when you need a specified decimal precision.

docs.title: Condition
docs.text:
Choose an output value according to a condition.

Configure

Open Conditions. Set Left value to Origin, Comparison to Greater, and Right value to the Number literal 0. Set Value when true to In stock and Value when false to Out of stock, both String literals.

Setting Example Conditions Compare Value when true Constant: In stock Value when false Constant: Out of stock

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = 3 "In stock"

Child area 1 is the condition tree. Select a condition and use 2 to set its mode, left/right values, comparison, and NOT. Groups use All or Any and contain child conditions. Choose OK to return.

Open Value when true, choose Literal, type String, and enter In stock. Value when false uses the same editor.

Notes

Either branch may use a literal, column, bind variable, origin, or earlier result. At runtime only the selected branch value is evaluated. Use numeric types on both sides when you want a numeric comparison.

docs.title: CodeMap
docs.text:
Translate codes between systems.

Configure

Open Code mapping. Map input code 1 to the String Active and code 0 to Inactive. Set Action when unmatched for values absent from the table.

Setting Example Ignore case False Code mapping 2 Settings Action when unmatched Fail

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = "1" "Active"

Use child area 1 to enter input codes and typed outputs, then 2, OK, to return. A row’s trash icon removes that mapping.

Notes

Unmatched actions are Fail, Keep, Null, and Default. Default lets you specify a replacement. Input codes must be unique, considering Ignore case. Treat codes with meaningful leading zeros as strings in both input and mapping.

docs.title: Coalesce
docs.text:
Select the first non-NULL candidate from a list.

Configure

Open Values to concatenate and list VALUE, BACKUP_EMAIL, then the String literal unknown@example.com. For Coalesce, this field holds candidates; it does not concatenate strings.

Setting Example Values to concatenate 3 Settings

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = NULLBACKUP_EMAIL = "backup@example.com" "backup@example.com"

In child area 1, set the mode, reference, literal type, and value as applicable; use 2, OK, to return. Column and Bind references use the dropdown. Literal values do not use Reference.

Notes

Candidates are evaluated in order until a non-NULL value is found. Empty and whitespace-only strings count as values. If all candidates are NULL, the result is NULL. Numbers and earlier step results are also supported.

docs.title: ConditionResult
docs.text:
Output whether a condition is true or false.

Configure

Open Conditions, choose All, and add two comparisons: Origin GreaterOrEqual 100 and Origin Less 200.

Setting Example Conditions All

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = 120 True

Child area 1 is the condition tree. Select a condition and use 2 to set its mode, left/right values, comparison, and NOT. Groups use All or Any and contain child conditions. Choose OK to return.

Notes

The result is a Boolean, not a string. Unlike Condition, it has no true/false output-value branches. Groups support All/Any and Negate (NOT). A later step can reference this Boolean result.

docs.title: Masking
docs.text:
Hide all or part of a name, phone number, or code with a chosen character.

Configure

Choose Keep trailing, set Trailing characters to keep to 4, and Mask character (1 character) to *. Use Keep leading or Keep leading and trailing for other partial masks. Only relevant length fields are shown.

Setting Example Masking mode Keep trailing Trailing characters to keep 4 Mask character (1 character) *

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = "09012345678" "*******5678"

Notes

The defaults are Mask all and *. Retain counts must be nonnegative. If their sum reaches the input length, the whole input is masked. NULL and empty strings stay unchanged. Lengths count Unicode code points without splitting surrogate pairs; combining marks count separately. The mask character follows the single-character padding restriction and cannot be a surrogate pair.

Mode Input Output Mask all 山田太郎 **** Keep 2 leading AB123456 AB****** Keep 4 trailing 09012345678 *******5678 Keep 1 leading and 2 trailing abcdef a***ef Short input with 4 trailing retained 123 ***

docs.title: When the retained length reaches or exceeds the input
docs.text:
The entire input is masked without an error, including when the retained length exactly equals the input length. The On conversion error policy is not invoked. For input 12345 and mask character *, the results are:

Configuration Output Keep 2 leading characters 12*** Keep 4 leading characters 1234* Keep 5 leading characters (equal length) ***** Keep 56 leading characters (exceeds input length) ***** Keep 1 leading and 4 trailing characters (total 5) *****

Keep leading and trailing uses the sum of both counts. This prevents a short input value from being exposed in full.

docs.title: Hashing
docs.text:
Produce a fixed-length hash string for matching equal input values.

Configure

Choose HMAC-SHA256 (SDI management key). Key source is fixed to SDI management key, so no additional key registration or input is needed. Choose SHA-256 (unkeyed) for an unkeyed calculation.

Setting Example Hash algorithm HMAC-SHA256 (SDI management key) Key source SDI management key

Try it

Sample input Final result VALUE = "employee001" "9c93a8ee3b2e26ba914428bf142fe552f383d8c01e7fdd362b0c58c906602c16"

Notes

UTF-8 input produces 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. NULL stays NULL; an empty string is hashed. Whitespace and case are preserved; normalize in earlier steps when needed. Use a string destination of at least 64 characters. HMAC results depend on the SDI configuration; the screenshot uses a sample environment. Unkeyed SHA-256 allows candidate values to be hashed and compared.

docs.title: Choosing a hash algorithm
docs.text:
Algorithm Inputs to the calculation Result for the same input Typical use HMAC-SHA256 (SDI management key) Input value and a key derived internally by SDI Identical with the same SDI configuration Pseudonymizing and matching identifiers SHA-256 (unkeyed) Input value only Identical across SDI environments Matching standard hashes with other systems

Neither algorithm requires additional hash-key registration. HMAC-SHA256 uses the existing SDI management-key mechanism. Use the default HMAC-SHA256 to conceal values such as employee IDs or phone numbers. With unkeyed SHA-256, candidates for the original value can be hashed and compared.

docs.title: Try unkeyed SHA-256
docs.text:
Change Hash algorithm to SHA-256 (unkeyed). Key source is hidden. Set the sample Input type to String and its value to abc, then click Preview conversion.

Sample input Result abc ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad

For this exact string encoded as UTF-8, the result is the same in every SDI environment.

docs.title: Output length and destination column
docs.text:
Both algorithms output exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, regardless of input length. Short input becomes longer; input longer than 64 characters becomes shorter.

Input Hash output length Employee ID E001: 4 characters 64 characters Phone number: 11 characters 64 characters Description: 1,000 characters 64 characters

Provide a string destination that can hold at least 64 characters; VARCHAR2(64 CHAR) is one Oracle example. SDI does not truncate the hash to fit the destination. NULL stays NULL; an empty string produces a 64-character hash.

docs.title: Consistent results across mappings and servers
docs.text:
Mappings and servers sharing the same SDI configuration produce the same result for the same input and transformation settings. Register the existing management key for the shared configuration on each server. Recreating the SDI configuration may change hash results.

Entering the same management password alone does not guarantee equal results in independently created SDI configurations. Share or migrate the same SDI configuration when hashes must match. The HMAC screenshot shows a sample environment, so its result may differ from yours.

docs.title: Saved settings and unavailable keys
docs.text: A mapping stores the algorithm, key source, and derivation version, never key material. If the HMAC key is unavailable, execution fails before extraction or output; the per-column NULL/default error policy does not apply. Hashing provides no reverse operation or absolute uniqueness guarantee.

docs.title: Transform separate columns and combine their results
docs.text:
Create these four steps. Steps 1–3 each read their own source column, keeping independent results.

Step Input Operation Result 1 VALUE = " ab " Trim "ab" 2 CODE = "xy" Upper "XY" 3 DATE = "20240401" DateTime "2024-04-01" 4 Results of steps 1, 2, 3 Concat, separator | "ab|XY|2024-04-01"

In step 4, choose StepResult for each concatenation item and select steps 1, 2, and 3 in order. Set Value to output to step 4 and preview.

Only earlier enabled steps can be referenced. Results not needed by the selected output or its dependencies are shown as not used. The calculation evaluates only required results and their dependencies. Results belonging to another target column are not available.

Back to column mapping settings

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Use SdiCli.exe to execute saved mappings, inspect configuration, validate and generate integration plans, apply settings, and review execution history. Specify an operation through commands and options. You can also execute a mapping by supplying only its name or ID.

The default installation folder is C:\Program Files\RiCCT\SimpleDataIntegrator. Run the examples from that folder or specify the full executable path.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Initialize SDI and register any required customer management keys in Studio first. CLI does not initialize settings or change management keys.

docs.title: Specify a command and options
docs.text:
SdiCli.exe mapping list --format json
SdiCli.exe mapping show --id M001 --format json
SdiCli.exe mapping exe --id M001 --request-id RUN-001 --format json
SdiCli.exe mapping exe --name "EMP_TO_EMPLOYEE" --request-id RUN-002 --format json

Replace sample IDs such as M001 with actual IDs. Specify exactly one of --id or --name. Names match exactly; ambiguous names require selection by ID before execution.

Reusing a --request-id returns the previous result instead of executing twice. Use a new ID for a different operation or an intentional rerun. If interruption leaves a result unknown, CLI does not retry automatically. Inspect execution logs before deciding what to do next. CLI cancellation through --timeout-seconds is not supported.

Manual mapping exe executes a mapping configured and saved in Studio, including mappings that use API input mapping or column value settings and transformations.

docs.title: Specify only a mapping name or ID
docs.text:
SdiCli.exe "EMP_TO_EMPLOYEE"
SdiCli.exe "MBE5B7F93B8E84B70B4D3AFDF229E1A35"

This format takes a single mapping name or ID. Additional options cannot be specified.

Exit code when supplying only a name or ID Meaning 0 Success 1 Execution failed 2 Mapping not found

docs.title: Command discovery and JSON results
docs.text:
SdiCli.exe system help --format json
SdiCli.exe system capabilities --format json
SdiCli.exe system inspect --format json

Use system help for commands, required arguments, and common options; system capabilities for supported features; and system inspect for the environment and license state. --format json selects an output format and does not enable AI mode.

JSON field Meaning schemaVersion / cliVersion Result schema and CLI versions action / caller Operation and caller mode, manual or ai status ok, needs_input, or error data Operation result issues / nextActions Errors, warnings, and required next steps operationId Execution identifier matching Studio logs. Omitted for operations without execution or errors before execution.

For the command-and-options format, exit code 0 means success. On a nonzero exit, inspect status and issues as well. For example, 3 requires revised input, 7 indicates integration failure, 8 an unknown execution result, and 9 an unsupported feature.

docs.title: Connections, metadata, and column suggestions
docs.text:
SdiCli.exe connection list --format json
SdiCli.exe connection show --id C001 --format json
SdiCli.exe connection test --id C001 --format json
SdiCli.exe metadata tables --connection-id C001 --schema public --format json
SdiCli.exe metadata columns --connection-id C001 --schema public --table emp --format json
SdiCli.exe schema get --name mapping-draft --format json
SdiCli.exe mapping suggest-columns --file mapping-draft.json --format json

Suggestions are not saved to operational settings automatically. Embedded MappingSpec metadata is matched offline; a side without metadata is inspected through its registered Connection. In a standalone MappingSpec, connectionRef is a registered Connection ID.

docs.title: Create, validate, and apply a plan
docs.text:
SdiCli.exe schema get --name integration-plan --format json
SdiCli.exe plan template --type table-merge --output plan.json --format json
SdiCli.exe plan validate --file plan.json --level static --format json
SdiCli.exe plan generate --file plan.json --mode draft --output-dir .\draft --format json

Edit the template for the real connections, tables, and column mappings. Static validation and draft generation do not connect to a database. A draft has not been checked against live metadata and cannot be applied directly.

Set passwords in an interactive terminal rather than writing plaintext into a plan. Do not combine this command with JSON output or redirection.

SdiCli.exe connection set-secret --plan-file plan.json --connection-ref source-db

Secrets use local references protected by the current user’s DPAPI. Configure them again when moving to another user or computer.

SdiCli.exe plan validate --file plan.json --level connected --format json
SdiCli.exe plan diff --file plan.json --level connected --format json
SdiCli.exe plan generate --file plan.json --mode deployable --output-dir .\generated --format json
SdiCli.exe plan apply --manifest .\generated\manifest.json --format json

Connected validation checks live database structures. Deployable generation creates settings and a manifest that can be applied. Keep generated files separate from the operational configuration folder. The apply command updates Connection, Mapping, and Scheduler settings and rechecks metadata, existing-setting hashes, and agreement between the plan and generated artifacts.

Saving is atomic per file and records a journal. If applying fails partway through, use the apply ID in the result to inspect and recover:

SdiCli.exe plan recover --apply-id APPLY001 --action inspect --format json
SdiCli.exe plan recover --apply-id APPLY001 --action rollback --format json

Keep Studio and Worker stopped until required recovery is complete. Rollback restores configuration files, not database data changed by an integration run.

docs.title: Schedules and execution history
docs.text:
SdiCli.exe schedule list --format json
SdiCli.exe schedule show --id S001 --format json
SdiCli.exe schedule preview --file plan.json --count 5 --format json
SdiCli.exe worker status --format json
SdiCli.exe execution list --mapping-id M001 --format json
SdiCli.exe execution show --id OPERATION_ID --format json
SdiCli.exe report generate --manifest .\generated\manifest.json --output-dir .\report --format json

Replace OPERATION_ID with the result’s operationId. Newly generated schedules are disabled. Preview times use the Worker’s local time and do not prove that a schedule ran or succeeded. Enabling an existing schedule requires its current configuration hash:

SdiCli.exe schedule set-enabled --id S001 --enabled true --expected-hash CURRENT_HASH --format json

Reports summarize information available when generated. They do not compare every data value or infer unavailable row counts.

docs.title: Calling CLI from AI
docs.text:
AI callers must add the value-less --ai flag:

SdiCli.exe mapping exe --id M001 --ai --request-id AI-RUN-001 --format json

AI-mode configuration changes and direct execution support a single-Worker configuration and require Studio closed and Worker stopped. CLI does not terminate them. While testing schedules through Worker, use CLI only to inspect status and history. CLI changes and executions use mutual exclusion in both manual and AI modes.

system inspect exposes the edition, valid, status, and aiUsePermitted under data.license. License terms permit AI use with a valid Developer or Enterprise license. An unavailable license is not treated as Developer. CLI does not itself block commands by edition, so also verify the applicable license terms.

docs.title: Scope of configuration generation and AI operations
docs.text:
Area Supported scope Connections and metadata Local Oracle 12c+ and PostgreSQL 12+. New Connections use Basic authentication. Mapping generation Table extraction; full, filtered, or timestamp-incremental data; Append, Merge, and delete plus Append. Scheduler generation Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Repeat. Outside scope Generating arbitrary transformation expressions or API input mappings; CustomSQL; configuration generation or AI operations for other databases; cluster changes; starting/stopping Worker; generic dry-run; execution cancellation.

This table covers CLI configuration generation and operations with --ai. To run a saved mapping manually, see Execute a saved mapping.

docs.title: Find a Mapping ID
docs.text: Choose the detail icon in the home form’s mapping list, then read Mapping ID in the detail form. You can also find IDs through mapping list.

docs.text: Stop CLI executions and wait for completion before creating or changing management keys. If settings are missing or a key cannot be read, follow System Settings recovery.

docs.text:
Set a shared password for people using Studio. Authentication is disabled by default. From the home form, open Preferences → Studio startup password authentication.

No Item Description 1 Enable password authentication Use the switch: blue is ON and gray is OFF. Select Save to apply the setting. 2 Current password Shown when authentication is enabled. Required to change or disable authentication. 3 New password Enter a password when enabling authentication or changing the password. 4 Confirm new password Enter the same new password again. 5 Save Validate input and save authentication settings.

docs.title: Enable authentication
docs.text:
1. Turn on the Enable password authentication switch.
  2. Enter the new password twice and select Save.
  3. Enter this password when starting Studio.

Use at least 6 characters. There are no character-type restrictions: Japanese characters, symbols, and spaces are allowed. Passwords are case-sensitive, and leading or trailing spaces are significant.

docs.title: Change the password or disable authentication
docs.text:
Action Steps Change the password Leave the switch ON. Enter the current password and the new password twice, then select Save. Disable authentication Turn the switch OFF. Enter the current password, then select Save. A new password is not required.

Changing the switch alone does not apply the setting. Select Cancel before saving to discard changes and close the form.

During saving, a wait cursor and Saving settings. Please wait. are displayed. Buttons and input fields are disabled. If an error appears, review it and retry.

1 marks the saving message; 2 marks the disabled Saving... button.

docs.title: Start Studio
docs.text:
When authentication is enabled, enter the Studio authentication password before the home form opens. Select OK to authenticate and open the home form. Select Cancel to exit Studio.

No Item Description 1 Password input Enter the Studio authentication password. The input is masked. 2 OK Verify the password and continue after successful authentication. 3 Cancel Exit Studio during startup, or keep values hidden when confirming a password reveal.

docs.title: Reveal passwords or keys
docs.text:
When Studio authentication is enabled, the following actions require the Studio authentication password each time values are revealed, including after successful startup authentication. Canceling the confirmation keeps values hidden.

Form Reveal control Values Connection configuration Show passwords and secrets Passwords, API keys, and other secrets Mail settings Show passwords and secrets SMTP password Mapping mail processing details Show beside the ZIP password Attached ZIP file password Customer-managed key configuration Show keys Management keys entered in the form

docs.title: Failed attempts and lockout
docs.text:
Consecutive failed attempts Lock duration 1–4 None 5–6 1 minute 7–8 5 minutes 9 or more 15 minutes

Startup, password reveal, and authentication settings use the same failure counter. Studio processes using the same local configuration share this counter, which survives Studio restarts. Expiration of a lock does not reset the count; successful authentication resets it to zero. Attempts during a lock neither authenticate nor increase the counter.

docs.title: Storage, backup, and recovery
docs.text:
Authentication settings are local to this computer. Configure Studio authentication on each computer, even when using a shared configuration folder. The authentication password is not stored as plaintext and is managed independently of sensitive-data encryption keys.

The storage folder is %ProgramData%\RiCCT\Sdi. The usual file locations are:

C:\ProgramData\RiCCT\Sdi\SdiWorkerBasic.config
C:\ProgramData\RiCCT\Sdi\StudioAuthentication.config

Enter %ProgramData%\RiCCT\Sdi in the File Explorer address bar to open the folder. Back up these two files as a pair. If saving is interrupted, the next Studio startup checks the saved state and performs recovery automatically when needed.

If you forget the password or see “An invalid operation was detected. Please contact support.”, contact support. Do not manually edit or delete these files.

Unattended Worker and CLI executions do not require the Studio authentication password. Upgrade Studio, Worker, and CLI together.

docs.title: System architecture
docs.text:
Simple Data Integrator (SDI) is composed by SDI Studio and SDI Worker agent. SDI Studio is a tool for configuring connections, mappings, schedules and parameters. The SDI Worker agent (Windows Service) is a tool that executes scheduled tasks. The SDI Gateway Service provides a proxy to access the remote database.

The SDI command line interface (SdiCli.exe) is also provided for the execution of mapping tasks from the command line.

docs.title: System Settings
docs.text: Use System Settings to configure the configuration folder, execution logs, sensitive data encryption, and the local Worker agent. Open Preferences → System Setting.

docs.title: Settings form
docs.text:
The image uses sample settings. Primary/Secondary and Failover Threshold appear when High Availability is enabled.

No Item Description 1 Configuration file folder Stores connections, mappings, and schedules. Computers sharing a configuration must access the same shared folder. 2 Sensitive Data Encryption Select a system-managed or customer-managed key as described below. 3 Change key Opens the key change dialog when customer-managed mode is selected. 4 Execution log folder Select the execution log location. 5 Log keep days Specify how many days to retain logs. 6 Agent List Review registered agents and remove obsolete registrations. 7 Worker Agent Name Set the display name of the agent on this computer. 8 High Availability Switch between a single agent and a Primary/Secondary configuration. When enabled, select the role and the inactivity threshold in minutes for failover. 9 Save Save changes. Follow any restart instructions displayed. 10 Close Close the settings form.

docs.title: Sensitive data encryption
docs.text:
Mode Use Operational requirements System-managed key A configuration used on one computer The key is computer-specific. Copying the configuration folder to another computer is insufficient. Customer-managed key Multiple computers or clusters Register the same key on every computer using the shared configuration.

A customer-managed key must contain 16–128 characters and is case-sensitive. It cannot be viewed later, so copy it when entering or generating it and retain it using your organization's key storage process.

The mode is determined from the identity information (ClientId) in the selected folder's shared SdiSystem.config. Each computer stores its key locally in SdiWorkerBasic.config, protected by Windows DPAPI. Use Studio to change modes rather than editing these files manually.

docs.title: Set or change a customer-managed key
docs.text:
This image shows rotation of an existing customer-managed key. Initial setup does not require the current key. Re-registration does not display new-key confirmation or generation.

No Item Description 1 Current customer-managed key Enter the current key when changing it. 2 New customer-managed key Enter the new key. 3 Confirm new key Enter the same new key again. 4 Generate Generate a key and fill the new-key and confirmation fields. 5 Copy Copy the new key. 6 Show keys Show or hide key values in this dialog. 7 OK Validate the input and close the dialog. Also save the System Settings form. 8 Cancel Close the key dialog.
  1. Stop Workers and CLI executions on all computers and wait for active tasks to finish.
  2. Select customer-managed mode in System Settings, or select Change key to rotate an existing key.
  3. Enter the required keys and retain the new key.
  4. Select OK to validate, then Save in System Settings.
  5. On other computers, register the same key. Verify connections on every computer before restarting Workers or CLI executions.

docs.title: Changing the configuration folder
docs.text:
The mode selection updates to match the selected folder. A new empty folder is displayed as system-managed.

Studio validates the selected folder's key and requests a customer-managed key if needed. Failed validation or cancellation restores the previous selection. Selecting and validating a folder does not rewrite its existing shared settings; use Save to apply the change.

docs.title: Initialization, recovery, and backup
docs.text:
Use Studio for initial configuration creation. Worker and CLI do not initialize settings.

If a management key or ClientId cannot be read, use the recovery dialog to re-register the customer-managed key, select another configuration folder, or contact support. Preserve the existing key and configuration files during recovery.

Back up the configuration folder and each computer's local settings, and retain the customer-managed key separately. Local settings are protected for their computer, so copying them does not replace key registration on a different computer.

If settings changed concurrently, restart Studio or reload settings, then repeat the operation using the latest state.

Initial startup and management keys
docs.text: Initialize settings in Studio on this computer before starting Worker for the first time. Worker does not create settings or management keys. Before changing keys, stop all Workers and CLI executions and wait for active tasks to finish. For multiple computers, register the same customer-managed key on each before resuming. See System Settings.

docs.title: Windows service operations
docs.text: The operation menu provides Open Services, Start Service, Stop Service, and Restart Service for SimpleDataIntegratorWorker. Availability depends on the current user's permissions. Agent start/stop and Windows service start/stop are different operations; wait for executing tasks to finish before maintenance.
